usageNotes: Use this to create a new VM by cloning an existing VM or template; it returns a task UPID string that you must poll (via get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status) to confirm completion before using the clone. For normal VMs a full disk copy is always performed, while templates default to a linked clone unless `full: true` is set — linked clones require the source to remain intact and on the same storage. Cross-node cloning (`target`) is only permitted when the source VM's disks reside on shared storage visible to both nodes.

examples.summary: Full clone of a template (VM 9000) to a new VM (101) on local-lvm, placed on the same node

tips: The returned string is a UPID (e.g. UPID:pve01:...). Poll get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status until status is 'stopped' and exitstatus is 'OK' before starting or reconfiguring the clone.
Linked clones (default for templates) share base disk blocks with the source — deleting or moving the source template will break linked clones. Use full: true if the source template may change.
Cross-node cloning requires shared storage (e.g. Ceph, NFS); disks on node-local storage cannot be cloned to a different target node.
If you specify `snapname`, the clone is created from that snapshot's disk state rather than the current disk state.

The caller needs VM.Clone on the source, VM.Allocate on the new VMID (or pool), Datastore.AllocateSpace on the target storage, and SDN.Use on any attached bridge/vnet — missing any of these returns a 403.
